Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop <n>of Milan.</n>
<r>7th Bk. on Luke, ch. xii</r>
<c>A</c>fter the condemnation of the Jewish people, the mystery of the Church is plainly declared in the figures of the repentant Ninevites, and of the Queen of the South. Like that Queen, the Church cometh from the uttermost parts of the earth, to hear the wisdom of the true Solomon, the Prince of Peace. <c>L</c>astly, the sign of the Prophet Jonas, as it was a figure of the Lord's sufferings, was also a witness to the gravity of those sins which the Jews committed. At the same time, we see in these words of the Lord a declaration at once of His power, and of His love; for, by turning our eyes on the Ninevites, He showeth us a way of escape, while He setteth before us the horror of what will otherwise be our punishment. Even the Jews need not cease to hope for pardon, if only they would repent.

b.050b61f3bd:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>uodécimo Kaléndas Mártii Luna duodécima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>H</h>ierosólymis natális sancti Simeónis, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui fílius Cleóphæ et propínquus Salvatóris secúndum carnem fuísse tráditur. Hic, Hierosolymórum Epíscopus post Iacóbum, fratrem Dómini, ordinátus, et, in Traiáni persecutióne, multis supplíciis afféctus, martýrio consummátus est, ómnibus qui áderant et Iúdice ipso mirántibus ut centum vigínti annórum senex fórtiter constantérque supplícium crucis pertulísset.
<h>A</h>pud Ostia Tiberína sanctórum Mártyrum Máximi et Cláudii fratrum, et Præpedígnæ, uxóris Cláudii, cum duóbus fíliis Alexándro et Cútia; qui, cum essent præclaríssimi géneris, omnes, iubénte Diocletiáno, tenti atque in exsílium deportáti sunt, ac deínde, incéndio concremáti, Deo ipsi odoríferum martýrii sacrifícium obtulérunt. Eórum relíquiæ, in flumen proiéctæ et a Christiánis perquisítæ, iuxta eándem civitátem sepúltæ sunt.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Lúcii, Silváni, Rútuli, Clássici, Secundíni, Frúctuli et Máximi.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Flaviáni Epíscopi, qui, cum fidem cathólicam Ephesi propugnáret, ab ímpii Dióscori factióne pugnis et cálcibus percússus est, et, in exsílium actus, ibídem post tríduum vitam finívit.
<h>T</h>oléti, in Hispánia, sancti Helládii, Epíscopi et Confessóris, qui a sancto Ildefónso, Toletáno Epíscopo, multis láudibus celebrátur.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.48730588e7:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>F</c>ebruary 18th 2027, the 12th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Jerusalem, the blessed martyr Simeon, Bishop of that holy city [from the year 46 to the year 107.] This is he of whom it is recorded that he was the son of Cleophas and the kinsman of the Saviour according to the flesh. He was ordained Bishop of Jerusalem next after James, the brother of the Lord. In the persecution under Trajan he was put to many torments and suffered martyrdom, and the judge and all men marvelled to see with how great boldness and firmness he endured the grievous torment of the cross at his great age, for he was an hundred and twenty years old.
<h>A</h>t Ostia, the holy brethren Maximus and Claudius, and Praeperdigna, the wife of Claudius, and their two sons, Alexander and Cutias, all martyrs, [in the year 295.] They were a very noble race, and by command of the Emperor Diocletian they were arrested and sent into exile, then they were consumed with fire, and so offered a sacrifice of sweet savour unto God himself. Their relics were cast into the river, but the Christians sought for them and buried them hard by the city.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Lucius, Sylvan, Rutulus, Classicus, Secundinus, Fructulus, and Maximus.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, [in the year 449,] holy Flavian, Bishop of that see, who, because he defended the Catholic faith at Ephesus, was assailed by the followers of the wicked Dioscorus with cuffs and kicks, and sent into exile, where he died after three days.
<h>A</h>t Toledo, [in the year 631,] the holy Confessor Helladius, Bishop of that see.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Sicut fuit Ionas in ventre ceti tribus diébus et tribus nóctibus, ita erit Fílius hóminis in corde terræ.
b.851ee2e54b:
<h>Canticle: Magnificat</h>
<r>Ant.</r> As Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, * so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
<r>Canticle of the Blessed Virgin</r>
<r>Luke 1:46-55</r>
§00.83742356bc
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> As Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
b.22142e2ec4:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>M</c>entes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, lúmine tuæ claritátis illústra: ut vidére possímus quæ agénda sunt; et, quæ recta sunt, ágere valeámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.3a16884752:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee to cast thy bright beams of light upon our mind, that we may clearly see whatsoever things Thou wouldst have us to do, and have strength to do always that which is pleasing in thy sight.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
